title: Per-worktree dev containers: launcher, stub-engine test, docs
summary: Adds `.devcontainer/worktree-container`, a POSIX sh launcher that starts, execs into, names and stops one development container per git worktree. It mounts the worktree read-write at /workspace, the main clone's git directory read-write at its host path, and the shared `.git/config` read-only on top of it, passing GH_TOKEN by name only. A stub-engine shell test exercises the mount set, name uniqueness and the main-clone refusal, and `docs/development.md` gains a section describing coverage and limits.

nodes.label: Developer shell
nodes.subtitle: start / exec / stop / name
nodes.summary: The caller supplies a worktree path, an optional GH_TOKEN, and the command to run. Nothing in this change alters the caller; it only gains a new entry point.

nodes.label: worktree-container
nodes.subtitle: start | exec | stop | name
nodes.summary: New POSIX sh script. Parses the subcommand and optional worktree argument, refuses a main clone, computes the common git dir, derives the container name from folder name plus a cksum of the full path, and dispatches to the engine.

nodes.label: Worktree resolver
nodes.subtitle: rev-parse --show-toplevel / --git-common-dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the worktree root, rejects it when `.git` is a directory (a main clone), and resolves the shared git directory to a physical path so the mount matches what the worktree file names.

nodes.label: Container name deriver
nodes.subtitle: osf-wt-<folder>-<cksum>
nodes.summary: Builds the container name from the sanitised folder name plus a checksum of the full worktree path, so two worktrees with the same folder name never collide.

nodes.label: Run-args builder
nodes.subtitle: three -v mounts, -e GH_TOKEN
nodes.summary: Assembles the `run -d --init` invocation: the worktree at /workspace, the common git dir at its host path, the config file read-only over it, GH_TOKEN by name, and the image.

nodes.label: Container engine
nodes.subtitle: docker / OSF_CONTAINER_ENGINE
nodes.summary: Any Docker-compatible engine. The launcher uses only options both Docker and Podman share, though only Docker is exercised.

nodes.label: Dev container
nodes.subtitle: sleep infinity, -w /workspace
nodes.summary: One long-lived container per worktree, started detached and kept alive with `sleep infinity`; commands arrive through `exec -w /workspace`.

nodes.label: /workspace mount
nodes.subtitle: worktree, read-write
nodes.summary: The worktree itself, mounted read-write at /workspace, which is what makes the git wrapper and forced hooks path apply.

nodes.label: Shared .git mount
nodes.subtitle: common dir, read-write
nodes.summary: The main clone's git directory at its own host path, read-write, because a commit writes objects, refs and this worktree's own files there.

nodes.label: Config overlay
nodes.subtitle: .git/config, read-only
nodes.summary: The shared config file mounted read-only on top of the git directory, so no process in the container can change branch tracking or git town parents.

nodes.label: Image dev home
nodes.subtitle: HOME inside the container
nodes.summary: The image's own home for its dev user. No host home or login folder is mounted, so it disappears with the container.

nodes.label: Main clone .git
nodes.subtitle: objects, refs, worktree files
nodes.summary: The shared git directory of the main clone. The change makes it writable from inside the container for the first time.

nodes.label: Shared .git/config
nodes.subtitle: read-only from the container
nodes.summary: The one file the launcher deliberately protects; writes to it from inside the container fail with a busy device.

nodes.label: worktree-container.sh
nodes.subtitle: stub engine, 11 checks
nodes.summary: Shell test that puts a recording stub engine on OSF_CONTAINER_ENGINE, creates real worktrees in a temp repo, and asserts the mount set, the token-by-name pass, name uniqueness and the main-clone refusal.

nodes.label: development.md section
nodes.subtitle: One container per worktree
nodes.summary: New section documenting the mount table, the naming scheme, the build/start/exec/stop recipe, the worktree-scoped commit identity, token passing, and an explicit covered / not-covered list.

edges.label: start|exec|stop|name
edges.summary: The caller runs the script with a worktree path and, for exec, a command after `--`.
Every subcommand first resolves the worktree root and the shared git directory.
The name is computed before any engine call, so `name` needs no engine at all.
On `start`, when no container exists yet, the run arguments are assembled and handed to the engine.

edges.label: inspect / run / exec / rm
edges.summary: The launcher is a thin wrapper: it shells out to the engine for every lifecycle step and never talks to the container directly.

edges.label: run -d --init
edges.summary: The engine creates the detached container from OSF_IMAGE and keeps it alive with `sleep infinity`.

edges.label: exec -e GH_TOKEN -w /workspace
edges.summary: Each `exec` call carries the caller's current GH_TOKEN by name and runs the command in /workspace.
The worktree is the only read-write source tree the container sees.
The shared git directory is mounted at its host path so the worktree file's recorded path resolves unchanged.
The config file is layered read-only over the writable git directory.
HOME resolves inside the container; nothing from the host home is mounted.

edges.label: read-write
edges.summary: This is the change's real subject: the shared git directory becomes writable from inside the container so commits work, while the config stays protected.

edges.label: read-only
edges.summary: The overlay that keeps branch tracking and git town parents out of reach.
The test invokes the real script with a stub engine on OSF_CONTAINER_ENGINE and inspects the recorded arguments.

edges.label: stub on OSF_CONTAINER_ENGINE
edges.summary: A shell stub records each call and reports no existing container, so no engine or image is needed.
The new section documents the mount table, naming, usage recipe and the covered / not-covered list.
